name: trust
title: Trust and risk
summary: Trust and Risk's case file: reports of counterfeit goods, suspicious orders, fake reviews and abuse from customers, sellers, staff, brand owners and automated signals, with evidence, a risk score, an investigation workflow, enforcement recommendations routed to the team that owns the action, recorded enforcement with reasons, and appeals decided by someone other than the original decider. Trust recommends; Catalog, Seller Manager, Support, Finance and the other owners act.
owns: Trust reports (TR- references) with type, source, reporter, subjects (seller, product, offer, order, customer, review, message, application, claim), description and status
Evidence: automated checks with pass/warn/fail results, documents, photos, notes, linked records, evidence requests to the reported party with deadlines
Risk score (0–100) with contributing factors and a recorded override
Investigation workflow: assign, escalate, resolve with an outcome, dismiss with a reason, reopen, merge duplicates

Enforcement recommendations routed to owner teams (suspend product or offer, restrict or suspend seller, hold payout, inform customers, remove reviews, restrict customer messaging) and the owner's accept or decline with reason
Recorded enforcement with reason, parameters, effect on open orders and cases, execution confirmation and reversal
Appeals against trust enforcement (customers and sellers), reviewed by someone other than the decider; read-only mirror of seller restriction appeals that came from a trust report
Automated detection rules (review bursts, linked new accounts with mismatched payments, brand registry mismatches) that raise reports
Application risk assessments for Seller Manager (risk level, flags, recommendation)
What reporters see: status and outcome of reports they made, without revealing their identity to the reported party
notOwns: Executing actions: catalog (products), offers (offers), sellers (restrictions, suspensions and their appeals), customers (customer restrictions), reviews (content removal), finance (holds), orders (dispatch holds), support (customer outreach and cases), messaging (conversation locks)
Reports on individual reviews, answers and questions for ordinary moderation: reviews (it refers patterns to trust through reviews.content.referred)
Payment fraud scoring by the provider: payments (trust consumes its signals)

stateMachines.name: Trust report
stateMachines.notes: Resolve needs an outcome and a summary; it is blocked while a recommendation is still sent_to_owner (RECOMMENDATIONS_OPEN) unless the outcome is referred. Dismiss needs a reason and a reporter-facing message. Escalated = high risk or needs the Trust and Risk Manager / Business Owner. Merge moves subjects, evidence and reporters into the kept report.

stateMachines.name: Recommendation
stateMachines.notes: Route sends it to the owner team's queue (workqueues). Accept is done by someone holding the owner team's permission for that action (e.g. catalog.products.publish for suspend_product, sellers.accounts.restrict for restrict_seller, customers.accounts.act for customer restrictions) and records an Enforcement with the owner's reason. Decline needs a reason. Trust staff cannot accept their own recommendations (separate duties, plan ch. 18). Actions that no module executes on trust.enforcement.recorded (hold_payout, hold_dispatch, review_payments, refund_buyers, inform_customers, revoke_claim, request_identity_confirmation, other) are done by the owner in its own screen first; accepting them requires externalRef, the record the owner created there (hold id, approval ref, case ref, claim id...), otherwise EXTERNAL_REF_REQUIRED (decision D4). keep_reviews needs no externalRef.

stateMachines.name: Enforcement execution
stateMachines.notes: Confirmed when the owning module's event arrives carrying the enforcement id or the report id: suspend_product catalog.product.publication_changed; suspend_offer offers.offer.status_changed; restrict_seller sellers.seller.restricted; suspend_seller sellers.seller.suspended; warn_seller sellers.warning.issued (trustEnforcementId); remove_reviews reviews.moderation.decided (trustEnforcementId); lock_conversation messaging.conversation.locked (trustEnforcementId); restrict_customer_* customers.account.restricted; hold_payout finance.hold.placed (trustReportId, also when the hold was placed after an approval); hold_dispatch and review_payments orders.item.cancelled (trustReportId); refund_buyers returns.refund.approved (trustReportId); inform_customers support.case.opened (trustReportId). Those stay pending until the event arrives even when accepted with externalRef. Actions nothing can confirm (keep_reviews, revoke_claim, request_identity_confirmation, other) are applied when recorded. Reverse (appeal overturned or error) publishes trust.enforcement.reversed, which the executing modules consume to undo the action (customers, catalog, sellers, offers, reviews, messaging, advertising), and raises a enforcement_reversal work item in the owner team's queue so a person checks the undo (stopgap until every owner confirms reversals).

stateMachines.name: Evidence request
stateMachines.notes: Expiry is noted on the report as missing proof; it is not a decision by itself.

stateMachines.name: Trust appeal
stateMachines.notes: The reviewer must differ from the person who recommended and the person who accepted the enforcement (SAME_REVIEWER_NOT_ALLOWED). Mirrored seller appeals (source sellers) follow the sellers state machine and are read-only here.

endpoints.desc: Accept checks the owner's own permission for the action through access (e.g. catalog.products.publish, sellers.accounts.restrict, customers.accounts.act, finance.holds.place) and its approval limit; above the limit the accept is sent for approval: the recommendation stays sent_to_owner with approvalRequestId and the call answers 200 with `approval` (ApprovalInfo); access.approval.decided (approved) accepts it as the requester. Accept records an Enforcement and publishes trust.enforcement.recorded, which the owning module executes. Actions no module executes (hold_payout, hold_dispatch, review_payments, refund_buyers, inform_customers, revoke_claim, request_identity_confirmation, other) are done in the owning module's screen first (e.g. Finance places the hold in admin/finance with the trustReportId) and accepted with externalRef; without it the accept is refused with EXTERNAL_REF_REQUIRED (alreadyApplied=true in the event so nobody executes it twice). Their enforcement is applied when the owning module's confirming event arrives (see the Enforcement execution machine) or at once when nothing can confirm it.

APPEAL_ALREADY_OPEN.meaning: An appeal for this enforcement is already open

NOT_APPEALABLE.meaning: This action cannot be appealed (e.g. informing customers)

APPEAL_IN_SELLERS.meaning: Seller account restrictions and suspensions are appealed and decided in sellers

SAME_REVIEWER_NOT_ALLOWED.meaning: The reviewer recommended or accepted the original action

SEPARATE_DUTIES.meaning: Trust staff cannot accept their own recommendations; the owner team decides

RECOMMENDATIONS_OPEN.meaning: Recommendations are still waiting for their owner teams

DATASET_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: The trust queue cannot be exported: the reports module is off or refused the dataset

EXTERNAL_REF_REQUIRED.meaning: No module executes this action: do it in the owning module's screen first and accept with externalRef (the hold, case, claim or approval reference)

notes: Trust recommends, owners act (plan ch. 17): Catalog suspends products, offers handle offer removal, Seller Manager restricts sellers, Support informs customers, Finance holds payouts. The owner's acceptance in trust records the enforcement and publishes trust.enforcement.recorded; catalog, offers, sellers, customers, reviews, messaging and advertising execute it and their own events confirm execution.

Owner modules that do not consume trust.enforcement.recorded (finance holds, orders dispatch holds, payments reviews, buyer refunds, support outreach, storefront claims, identity confirmation) act in their own screens; the owner then accepts the recommendation with externalRef, which is required for these actions (decision D4; EXTERNAL_REF_REQUIRED), and the event carries alreadyApplied=true so nobody executes it twice. Executing actions take an optional trustReportId so trust can confirm them: catalog setPublication, sellers createRestriction / suspendSeller / warnings (sellers.seller.restricted / suspended, sellers.warning.issued), finance placeHold (finance.hold.placed), orders cancel-items (orders.item.cancelled), customers account actions (customers.account.restricted), returns exception refunds (returns.refund.approved) and support staff cases (support.case.opened).

Executing modules confirm with the enforcement id they were given: sellers.warning.issued, reviews.moderation.decided and messaging.conversation.locked carry trustEnforcementId; remove_reviews, warn_seller and lock_conversation are no longer applied on record. keep_reviews stays applied on record; reviews closes the open moderation items on the named content as kept.

Reversals (decision D9): trust.enforcement.reversed carries the action, typed params, targets and the appliedRef so each executing module undoes exactly what it did (customers lifts the restriction, catalog republishes, sellers lifts the restriction or ends the suspension, offers reinstates the offer, reviews reinstates removed content, messaging unlocks, advertising resumes). Until every owner confirms its undo, trust also raises a enforcement_reversal work item in the owner team's queue (dedupe trust_reversal:<enforcementId>), closed by the owner by hand.
Offer suspension is owned by the Catalog Manager (decision D8): suspend_offer routes to the catalog team, is accepted with offers.offers.remove and is executed by offers.
Valid order history and access to help are preserved for everyone involved in every enforcement (plan ch. 17); each recorded effect list states what keeps working.
Reporters are never revealed to reported parties. Reports on reviews, answers and questions stay in reviews; the account/reviews 'Reports you made' tab merges both lists.

Appeals: trust decides appeals on its enforcement (offers, products, claims, customer restrictions from trust). Seller account restrictions and suspensions are appealed and decided in sellers; trust mirrors linked ones read-only so the Trust and Risk Manager sees them in one Appeals tab.

Approval actions registered with access: trust.enforcements.reverse (authority). Approval limits for the executed actions (holds, restrictions) belong to the owning module's action and are checked at accept time.

Phase 2: rights-owner reports through the public form and stronger moderation tooling; automated detection, evidence, recommendations, enforcement and appeals are phase 1 because the admin/trust screen and the launch checklist depend on them.
Exports: trust registers dataset trust.admin.reports with reports.registerDataset and serves the rows through exportRows; reporter identity columns need trust.reports.export-identities.
